main_text.p: cuatione per superiora & inferiora, puella tandem conualuit. Quoniam autem huius alexipharmaci tanta uis est, & admiranda aduersus omnia propemodum genera uenenorum, idcirco ipsum describere haud pigebit nos, licet in symphonijs Galeni, Pauli Æginetæ, & aliorum medicorum, Græcorum libri secundi, ἀντιφαρμάκων[?] Dioscoridis extet. Recipit radicis Valerianæ feminuncia, radicis Asclepiadis unciã: polypodij quercini, altheæ, angelicæ sylueftris singulorum uncias duas: angelicæ satiuæ recentis uncias quatuor: corticis radicum Laureolæ sexcunciam. Radices hæ omnes effodiendæ sunt eo tempore, quod quintum decimum Augusti, & octauum Septembris intercedit, ipso authore Moibano: Veruntamen tardius illas effoderunt nonnulli postea, qui nihilominus efficacissimam effecerunt antidotum. Deinde incisæ imponā-tur in uitreatam ollā, affuso aceto perquàm acri, quod duobus digitis radices excedat. Tum olla opercula clausa, rimęq; omnes oui albo cum polline subacto acurate oblinantur. Posthæc in ipsa olla ad lentum ignem parum bulliant. Dein aperta olla, & abiecto aceto, quod redundat, radices exiccen-tur,

page.notes: The Greek word in the second-to-last line of the first paragraph ("ἀντιφαρμάκων") is a best guess from a small, blurred print; it is marked [?]. Printed "fyluestris" and "fatiuæ" were read with plain s. "Tum olla" and "Dein aperta" run on in the same paragraph; no printed indent begins a new paragraph on this page. No printing errors were otherwise identified.
